# Miqsat Ma'ase Ha-Torah Section 6 — The LOGOS Bible (Formal)
**Translator:** LOGOS | **Source:** 4QMMT (4Q394–399, Cave 4), Section C | **Condition:** Fragmentary; reconstructed from multiple manuscripts

---

**6:1** And you know that no treachery or deceit or evil is found in our hand, since for [these matters] we offer [...]

**6:2** [...] And indeed we write to you [...] for your benefit and for the benefit of your people [...]

**6:3** [...] for we perceived that you possess wisdom and knowledge of the Torah. Consider [...]

**6:4** [...] all the things that have come upon you [...] and you will discover [...]

**6:5** [And in]deed we have [written] to you some of the works of the Torah which we believe to be good for you and for your people, for we perceived that you possess wisdom and knowledge of the Torah.

**6:6** Consider all these things and petition Him to direct your counsel aright and to keep far from you evil scheming and the counsel of Belial,

**6:7** so that you may rejoice at the end of time, when you discover that some of our words are true.

**6:8** And it shall be reckoned to you as righteousness, when you do what is right and good before Him, for your benefit and for the benefit of Israel.

**6:9** [...] for [...] in the Book of Moses it is written [...] and in the words of the Prophets [...]

**6:10** [...] that the blessings came [...] in the days of Solomon the son of David [...] and also the curses [...]

**6:11** [...] that came from the days of Jeroboam the son of Nebat until the exile of Jerusalem and Zedekiah king of Judah [...]

**6:12** [...] that He will bring upon them [...] and it is written [...] in the Book of Moses and in the [words of the] Prophets that [...]

**6:13** [...] [the bles]sings came in the days of David and Solomon [...] and the curses came from [...] until [...]

**6:14** [...] and we recognize that some of the blessings and the curses that are written in the Book of [Moses] have already come to pass [...]

**6:15** And this is the end of days, when they shall return in Israel for[ever ...] and shall not turn back [...]

**6:16** [...] but the wicked shall act [...] and [...] remember [...]

**6:17** Remember the kings of Israel and contemplate their deeds: whoever among them revered [the To]rah was delivered from troubles;

**6:18** those were the seekers of the Torah whose transgressions were forgiven.

**6:19** Remember David, who was a man of pious deeds, and he too was delivered from many troubles and was forgiven.

**6:20** And moreover we have written to you some of the works of the Torah [...] that it might be for your benefit [...]

**6:21** [...] for [...] you shall receive [...] at the end of time [...] when you walk in uprightness before Him [...]

**6:22** [...] and it shall be reckoned to you as righteousness [...] for doing what is upright and good before Him [...]

**6:23** [...] for your benefit and for the benefit of Israel [...]

**6:24** [...] and it is written: [...] at the end of days [...]

**6:25** [...] and remember all the words of Moses, the servant of God [...]

---

*LOGOS notes: Section C constitutes the theological and rhetorical apex of MMT. The phrase "it shall be reckoned to you as righteousness" (6:8, 6:22) is of extraordinary significance for biblical theology, echoing Gen 15:6. LOGOS renders this in formal liturgical register to mark its theological weight. "Revered the Torah" (6:17) elevates EMET's "feared" to capture the reverence-dimension of yare'. The deuteronomistic history is invoked: Solomon (blessings), Jeroboam-to-Zedekiah (curses). "Seekers of the Torah" (dorshei ha-torah) is a technical sectarian designation preserved in formal English. David as "a man of pious deeds" (ish chasadim) connects to the project's rendering of chesed-related vocabulary. The document's conclusion reiterates its central appeal: Torah faithfulness yields righteousness.*
